title: The Carbon Count Pays the Bill

scenes.tts: How can a leaf pull carbon from air, build sugar, and still keep its carbon-catching machine running? Follow the carbon count, and the energy bill will reveal itself.
scenes.visual: Open inside one large schematic chloroplast that fills the frame: a pale stroma surrounds one thick circular conveyor, with a green five-counter RuBP carrier circulating clockwise. A blue carbon dioxide counter drifts in from outside while an empty gold sugar-output tray waits at right. During the first question, the counter approaches the loop, the carrier keeps circling, and question marks grow over both the output tray and the returning-carrier position. During the second sentence, a bright counting bracket sweeps across the counters and two small ATP/NADPH meters slide up from the bottom. Keep the conveyor and drifting stroma particles moving throughout; use no molecular structures. On-screen labels are at least 28 px and name only 'CO2', 'RuBP · 5C', 'sugar output', 'ATP', and 'NADPH'.
scenes.narration: How can a leaf pull carbon from air, build sugar, and still keep its carbon-catching machine running? Follow the carbon count, and the energy bill will reveal itself.

scenes.visual: Do not cut away from the chloroplast world. Dim the still-moving conveyor slightly, transform the two question marks into the centered title 'The Carbon Count Pays the Bill', and draw a short gold rule beneath it. The carbon dioxide counter continues drifting toward RuBP behind the title. Fade the title before the two seconds end so the same conveyor is ready for the next scene.

scenes.tts: The Calvin cycle runs in chloroplast stroma, using A T P and N A D P H from light reactions.
scenes.caption: The Calvin cycle runs in chloroplast stroma, using ATP and NADPH from light reactions.
scenes.visual: Return the conveyor to full brightness. Before 'chloroplast stroma', briefly outline the chloroplast and wash the surrounding interior teal, then settle the label 'stroma' in the open space above the loop. Along the left edge, a schematic thylakoid bar pulses softly and sends one ATP block and one NADPH block toward the conveyor as they are named. Replace the five-dot RuBP icon with five large numbered carbon counters locked into a rounded carrier; keep the carrier moving clockwise and the incoming carbon dioxide counter bobbing gently.
scenes.narration: The Calvin cycle runs in chloroplast stroma, using ATP and NADPH from light reactions.

scenes.tts: Rubisco joins one carbon dioxide to RuBP, a five-carbon acceptor. The brief six-carbon intermediate immediately splits into two three-carbon molecules of three-phosphoglycerate, or three P G A. Fixation itself spends no A T P or N A D P H.
scenes.caption: Rubisco joins one CO2 to RuBP, a five-carbon acceptor. The brief six-carbon intermediate immediately splits into two three-carbon molecules of 3-phosphoglycerate, or 3-PGA. Fixation itself spends no ATP or NADPH.
scenes.visual: Zoom the carried conveyor to fill at least 60% of frame height. A large schematic Rubisco clamp, labeled 'Rubisco', closes around the moving 'RuBP · 5C' carrier only when the blue 'CO2 · 1C' counter arrives. The six counters briefly ride together under a '6C · brief' bracket, then the carrier separates into two equal rounded blocks, each containing three counters and labeled '3-PGA · 3C'; the blue CO2 counter rides in only one of the two blocks. Keep both blocks gliding apart along the conveyor while a zero-cost stamp lands over the unchanged ATP and NADPH meters: 'ATP 0 · NADPH 0'. Do not draw bonds, atoms, or a molecular structure.
scenes.narration: Rubisco joins one CO2 to RuBP, a five-carbon acceptor. The brief six-carbon intermediate immediately splits into two three-carbon molecules of 3-phosphoglycerate, or 3-PGA. Fixation itself spends no ATP or NADPH.

scenes.tts: Both three P G A molecules must become the triose sugar G three P. Each conversion spends one A T P to prime the acid and one N A D P H to reduce it. So far, one carbon dioxide has cost two A T P and two N A D P H.
scenes.caption: Both 3-PGA molecules must become the triose sugar G3P. Each conversion spends one ATP to prime the acid and one NADPH to reduce it. So far, one CO2 has cost 2 ATP and 2 NADPH.
scenes.visual: Carry the two '3-PGA · 3C' blocks forward on parallel lanes of the same circular conveyor. As 'each conversion' is spoken, one ATP block and then one NADPH block slide into each lane; their meter counts tick down twice. Each 3-PGA block transforms in place into a gold 'G3P · 3C' block without changing its three visible carbon counters. On the final sentence, the lanes merge and a compact ledger rolls up beside them: '1 CO2 so far' above '2 ATP + 2 NADPH'. Keep the two G3P blocks orbiting slowly while the numbers settle.
scenes.narration: Both 3-PGA molecules must become the triose sugar G3P. Each conversion spends one ATP to prime the acid and one NADPH to reduce it. So far, one CO2 has cost 2 ATP and 2 NADPH.

scenes.tts: But can both new trioses leave while the conveyor keeps turning? Count the carbons needed to rebuild each five-carbon acceptor.
scenes.visual: At the output fork, animate both gold 'G3P · 3C' blocks beginning to leave toward the sugar tray. The circular conveyor keeps turning behind them; do not show it emptying, which would give away the answer. On the question, stop the departing blocks halfway and replace the ledger with large centered text: 'Can both leave?' Beneath it, show an empty five-slot RuBP carrier and a row of six movable carbon counters. The counters gently bob, inviting the viewer to count, while the conveyor continues crawling in the background.
scenes.narration: But can both new trioses leave while the conveyor keeps turning? Count the carbons needed to rebuild each five-carbon acceptor.

scenes.visual: Hold the exact question 'Can both leave?' and the empty five-slot RuBP carrier. For the deliberate thinking pause, let the six carbon counters bob one after another and let a thin highlight travel around the otherwise empty circular conveyor; make no answer appear. Keep all labels high-contrast and the question centered.

scenes.tts: Scale up to three turns. Three RuBP plus three carbon dioxides make six trioses, holding eighteen carbons altogether. Only three carbons came from air, so only one triose is net gain.
scenes.caption: Scale up to 3 turns. 3 RuBP plus 3 CO2 make 6 trioses, holding 18 carbons altogether. Only 3 carbons came from air, so only 1 triose is net gain.
scenes.visual: Resolve the pause by widening the same conveyor into a three-lane loop, not a new diagram. Three green 'RuBP · 5C' carriers and three blue 'CO2 · 1C' counters enter in synchronized motion; a large running counter climbs from 15 to 18 carbons. Transform them into six gold 'G3P · 3C' blocks circulating around the loop. When 'only three carbons came from air' is spoken, color exactly three counters blue across the six blocks. At 'one triose', guide one three-counter block into the output tray while the other five remain moving on the loop.
scenes.narration: Scale up to 3 turns. 3 RuBP plus 3 CO2 make 6 trioses, holding 18 carbons altogether. Only 3 carbons came from air, so only 1 triose is net gain.

scenes.tts: The other five trioses hold fifteen carbons, exactly enough to rebuild three five-carbon acceptors. The counters are reshuffled, not discarded. Regeneration then spends three more A T P to remake RuBP and close all three loops.
scenes.caption: The other 5 trioses hold 15 carbons, exactly enough to rebuild 3 five-carbon acceptors. The counters are reshuffled, not discarded. Regeneration then spends 3 more ATP to remake RuBP and close all 3 loops.
scenes.visual: Keep the one net G3P block parked in the output tray. The remaining five G3P blocks flow into a large translucent schematic shuffle drum on the same conveyor; their fifteen counters remain individually visible and tumble continuously. Open the drum to reveal three equal five-counter carriers, proving no counter vanished. Then send one ATP block into each carrier as its label transforms from '5C sugar' to 'RuBP · 5C'. The three rebuilt carriers rejoin the three-lane loop and pass beneath Rubisco while the ATP meter drops by three.
scenes.narration: The other 5 trioses hold 15 carbons, exactly enough to rebuild 3 five-carbon acceptors. The counters are reshuffled, not discarded. Regeneration then spends 3 more ATP to remake RuBP and close all 3 loops.

scenes.tts: Now divide that three-turn bill by three. At steady state, the ordinary C three cycle costs three A T P per carbon dioxide. It also costs two N A D P H. One extra A T P beyond reduction pays to rebuild the acceptor. Count the carbons, and the bill follows.
scenes.caption: Now divide that 3-turn bill by 3. At steady state, the ordinary C3 cycle costs 3 ATP per CO2. It also costs 2 NADPH. One extra ATP beyond reduction pays to rebuild the acceptor. Count the carbons, and the bill follows.
scenes.visual: Keep the three completed loops turning across the upper half. Build a ledger from the actual moving tokens below: first collect '6 ATP + 6 NADPH' under reduction and '3 ATP' under regeneration, then place a large division-by-three bar across both totals. Transform the result into 'per CO2: 3 ATP + 2 NADPH'. As 'one extra ATP' is spoken, move one of the three ATP icons onto a small returning-RuBP arrow, while two ATP and two NADPH icons remain beside the reduction lanes. On the final sentence, sweep a counting bracket around one full loop.
scenes.narration: Now divide that 3-turn bill by 3. At steady state, the ordinary C3 cycle costs 3 ATP per CO2. It also costs 2 NADPH. One extra ATP beyond reduction pays to rebuild the acceptor. Count the carbons, and the bill follows.

scenes.tts: Three turns therefore spend nine A T P and six N A D P H for one net G three P. Six turns spend eighteen A T P and twelve N A D P H for two net trioses. Those trioses can supply one hexose phosphate at the same Calvin-cycle cost. The plant does not directly release free glucose here.
scenes.caption: 3 turns therefore spend 9 ATP and 6 NADPH for 1 net G3P. 6 turns spend 18 ATP and 12 NADPH for 2 net trioses. Those trioses can supply 1 hexose phosphate at the same Calvin-cycle cost. The plant does not directly release free glucose here.
scenes.visual: Use the same conveyor as a working scale rather than cutting to a list. One lap marker expands to '3 turns' while nine ATP tokens and six NADPH tokens stream through the meters; one G3P block reaches the tray. Duplicate the moving three-turn group once, and let the lap marker roll to '6 turns', the meters to '18 ATP' and '12 NADPH', and the tray to two G3P blocks. Finally, slide those two labeled blocks together inside a dashed box labeled 'hexose phosphate supply'; add a small crossed-out label 'free glucose directly' as the last sentence lands.
scenes.narration: 3 turns therefore spend 9 ATP and 6 NADPH for 1 net G3P. 6 turns spend 18 ATP and 12 NADPH for 2 net trioses. Those trioses can supply 1 hexose phosphate at the same Calvin-cycle cost. The plant does not directly release free glucose here.

scenes.tts: This is the simplest steady-state picture. Startup, photorespiration, and carbon-concentrating pathways change the accounting; the page below develops those cases.
scenes.visual: Keep the conveyor turning at center and place a small high-contrast badge above it: 'simplest steady state'. Around the loop, introduce three compact edge cards one at a time, without replacing the world: a rising dawn gauge labeled 'startup', a Rubisco fork labeled 'photorespiration', and a carbon dioxide pump labeled 'C4 / CAM'. Each card gently moves—gauge rising, fork rocking, pump cycling—while the central carbon counters continue their ordinary path. End by shrinking the cards toward a downward arrow labeled 'deeper below', leaving the core loop unobscured.
scenes.narration: This is the simplest steady-state picture. Startup, photorespiration, and carbon-concentrating pathways change the accounting; the page below develops those cases.

scenes.tts: A leaf builds carbon product only while rebuilding its carbon catcher. That is why one triose in six is net, and why A T P demand exceeds N A D P H demand.
scenes.caption: A leaf builds carbon product only while rebuilding its carbon catcher. That is why 1 triose in 6 is net, and why ATP demand exceeds NADPH demand.
scenes.visual: Show the full chloroplast world again. One G3P block slides into the gold output tray while five return through the shuffle drum and become three RuBP carriers; synchronize both motions so output and rebuilding happen together. The conveyor makes one final continuous lap, and the ATP meter visibly sits one unit higher than the NADPH meter per carbon dioxide. As the last words land, transform the loop and meters into a single counting bracket framing the rule, then fade everything except the moving bracket.
scenes.narration: A leaf builds carbon product only while rebuilding its carbon catcher. That is why 1 triose in 6 is net, and why ATP demand exceeds NADPH demand.

scenes.visual: End card over the faintly turning conveyor: large centered line 'Count the carbons, and the bill follows.' with a short gold rule beneath it. Keep the highlighted carbon counter completing one slow lap behind the text so the frame never freezes. No title, subtitle, or extra claim appears.
